newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods hurt by NYMEX, diffs mixed.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods hurt by NYMEX, diffs mixed.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product prices were pounded by late Wednesday tracking December NYMEX futures, with gasoline and heating oil differentials steady to mostly weaker in subdued trade, players said.
Traders watched early NYMEX gains vanish, with prices veering into ever-more-negative territory on a technical selloff.

Initially, a bullish crude draw in the API's and EIA's weekly stocks report stoked the market higher. But by day's end, December gasoline stood 2.0 cents a gallon lower and heating oil had lost 1.59 cents.

On the cash side, few deals were spotted in the New York Harbor gasoline market, where offers on "M5" conventional unleaded gasolne slipped to about 1.85 cents over the print, almost a half cent weaker than Tuesday differentials.
"I got a lot of phone calls today from brokers who just wanted to talk, not to do any business," one East Coast trader said, noting a distinct lack of buying interest.

Other traders predicted gasoline diffs will endure more downward pressure after this week's restoration of catalytic crackers at PDVSA's Amuay refinery and Sun Oil's refinery in Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania.
